speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your pruritic rash in detail, including when it started and if it has spread. You also mentioned a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; have you noticed any other symptoms like sore throat or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rubella (German Measles). The combination of a fever followed by a spreading rash that starts on the face and then moves to the trunk and extremities, along with the specific description of the rash sparing the perioral area, is highly characteristic of Rubella.
